nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What are the four key values identified in the Gothenburg Consensus Statement for HIA?
nodes.answer: The four key values are democracy, equity, sustainable development, and ethical use of evidence.
nodes.paragraph: A sepa - rate, alternative world view uses knowledge generated through both quantitative and qualitative evidence and data, including sociological evidence such as interviews and real-world experience to create a picture of health impacts. This can create conflict in the field or lead to fractionalisation in perspectives around the theory and practice of HIA [ 12, 15]. Methodologies and perspec - tives have taken advantage of legislative drivers such as EIA integration and events such as the COVID-19 pan - demic to seize opportunities to include health and equity [16 18]. The Gothenburg Consensus Statement identified four key values for HIA: democracy, equity, sustainable devel - opment and ethical use of evidence [ 2]. These values were confirmed and expanded in the International Association for Impact Assessment (IAIA) published International Best Practice Principles for HIA, namely with Equity and Equality; Participation; Ethical use of evidence; Sustain - ability; and Comprehensive approach to health [ 19]. How these values are integrated into HIA guidance and prac - tice varies [ 20]. Reducing inequities is a core principle and part of most HIA definitions.

nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What additional step was taken after selecting the initial studies for analysis?
nodes.answer: The reference lists of the included articles were sought out to identify additional articles fitting within the research scope.
nodes.paragraph: A total of 42 studies were selected for full article screening. During the full article screening, each study was assessed individually for relevance to the literature search theme. At this stage, studies were excluded if they did not report original research (i.e. literature review studies). We also excluded studies that did not use quantitative environmental assessment methodologies (i.e. LCA and footprint method). It is important to note that relevant studies mentioned in literature review studies had already been identified dur - ing the screening process and no additional studies were discovered. Also, studies were excluded if the healthcare devices covered were not electronic. The full-text screen- ing ultimately resulted in a selection of fourteen studies. Furthermore, the reference lists of the included articles were sought out to identify additional articles that fit within the scope of the research. After abstract and/or full-text screen- ing of the studies from the reference list, three studies were selected, resulting in a final total of 17 studies included in the analysis. The entire search strategy is depicted in Fig. 1. 2.3 Extraction of information and in depth analysis Extraction of information from the 17 selected studies was performed according to predetermined criteria.

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the typical structure of Multicriteria Analysis (MCA)?
nodes.answer: The typical structure of MCA includes identifying relevant criteria and alternatives, assigning numerical values to indicate the importance of criteria, quantifying impacts of alternatives, and using a formal mathematical procedure for ranking the alternatives.
nodes.paragraph: Maleki et al. (2018) [ 28] apply Multicriteria-Spatial Decision Support System (MSDSS) for prioritization of wetland restoration using different scenarios. MCA has also been used for area prioritization through ranking of criteria. Valente et al. (2021) [29] used a mixed method of participatory analysis and multi-criteria evaluation to identify priority areas for forest restoration coupled with water related ecosystem services. The typical structure of MCA includes the identification of the relevant criteria and alter - natives from the existing theory and practice, the assignment of numerical values to criteria to indicate their relative importance and to quantify the impacts of the alternatives on these criteria, and the use of a formal mathematical procedure for analyzing numerical values to determine the ranking (priorities) of the alternatives [ 30]. The objective of this study is to present the development of a participatory and replicable MCA methodology and its application at in-person or online workshops, through a tool for identifying and prioritizing NBS/BES that cover the WEFE nexus and have a considerable impact on socio-economic parameters [ 2, 4].

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do concerns about quality and logistics impact ethical consumption in rental services?
nodes.answer: Concerns about quality and logistics can impact ethical consumption in rental services by affecting the perceived convenience, spontaneity, and organization required for renting items. These factors can influence consumer behaviour, especially when compared to the simplicity of purchasing fast fashion.
